claims.claim: For struggling learners, retain a step-by-step tutorial and an animated-GIF build alternative so the core program can be followed through more than one guided representation.
For advanced learners, reserve an explicit Extend phase after the core create-and-evaluate sequence, allowing a short lesson to offer stretch without making it a prerequisite for success.
Use the canonical lesson's extension-by-ability guidance to keep a common core task while offering optional challenges for learners who finish quickly.
Provide support and challenge as separate options around the same light-sensing if/then program, rather than replacing the introductory task for either group.
Pair support with stretch in the rock-paper-scissors lesson so all learners can complete the shake-and-random core while faster learners extend it.

Use a Think-Create-Evaluate-Extend-Share lesson arc with teacher notes and a recap so learners needing help receive repeated context while advanced learners have a defined point for independent extension.
